title: Enum Methods
story: The traffic light at the intersection cycles Red → Green → Yellow → Red. You want the TrafficLight itself to know how to advance to the next color — no separate function needed!
why: Enums can have methods, just like structs. This keeps behavior close to the type, making your code more organized and intuitive.
analogy: Enum methods are like buttons on a remote control. Each button (variant) does something different when pressed, and the remote knows which button was pressed and what to do next.
try_it: Add a `cycles_until_red` method that takes a starting color and counts how many `next()` calls it takes to reach Red. Test starting from Green (should take 1), Yellow (should take 2), and Red (should take 0).
tips: Enum methods use `self` just like struct methods — the first parameter is always `self`
Match on `self` inside the method to determine which variant you are
Methods can return a different variant — `next()` goes from Red to Green, changing the state
common_mistakes: Forgetting the enum prefix when returning: `return Green` is wrong — must be `return TrafficLight.Green`
Using `self` in match but writing `TrafficLight.Red` in the pattern — use bare names: `Red => { ... }`
Calling `next()` without reassigning: `light.next()` alone doesn't change `light`; you need `light = light.next()`
